contexts.text: Doctrines separated from the Church, or heresies. Treated of. AC 332. AC 337.
This heresy, amplified, is called Enoch.

Wherever there is any Church there arise heresies, because when people are thinking about one article of faith they make it the principal one; for man's thought is of such a nature that when it is fixed upon any one thing it sets it above all other things, especially when phantasy claims it as one's Own invention...
Ground = a schism or heresy.
To cultivate the ground = to cultivate this schism or heresy.
That this schism or heresy produced from itself another. Signified. AC 401.
From one heresy many are born.
The case was the same with the heresy called Cain. Explained.
By the names are signified heresies and doctrines.
Where is there any heresy which does not in this way find confirmations...
Many... who are in... any heresy suppose that all those who are outside of it... cannot be saved...
Those born in any heresy, who have confirmed themselves in its falsities... can with difficulty, if ever, be brought to receive truths which are contrary to their falsities.
When falsities have insinuated themselves into evils, schisms and heresies arise... If charity reigned... they would not call schism schism, nor heresy heresy, but a doctrinal matter of opinion...
That heresies and controversies... would resound. Signified.
Then heresies would be dissipated, and out of many they would make one Church...
They all fell into heresies and Falsities...
Preface. (This) is evident from so many heresies, of which each confirms his own dogma from the literal sense... AC 3427:3. AC 3436. AC 6222:2.
Heretical, occurs. DP 231:3.

All these things are the beginning of sorrows = the first state of the perversion of the Church, which is... that they begin no longer to know what good and truth are, but dispute together about them, whence come Falsities, and thus heresies.
This is evident from every heresy, and from each thing in a heresy, which, although they are falsities, by means of the confirmations of those who are in the heresy, appear to be truths.
Unless truths from the internal sense are insinuated into these scientifics (from the literal sense), the mind can be drawn away into every heresy... Example(s). AC 10276:8. LJ 1.
From such persons, who were in some truth from the Word, but not in good, have arisen all the heresies within the Church; for what is heretical appeared to them exactly like truth.
Those in heresy, or in no truth of faith, are here meant by the wrong doer.
If others (insinuate truth) heresies arise...
They who are in heresies and in a life of good...
As heretics who are conscientious and zealous are wont to do...
Hence so many and such great hallucinations and heresies.
Hence that infernal heresy...
All do so, even heretics.
Hence the Word is called by such the Book of heresies.
(Hence) so many heresies... because the leaders have regarded themselves...
Hence it is that so many heresies have arisen, and that by some the Word is called the Book of heresies...
Whence come ignorance, heresies, and errors.
Whence, otherwise, so many heresies from the same Word?
They who read the Word without doctrine are... yielding to heresies...
That heresies may be taken from the sense of the letter... but that to confirm them is hurtful. General article. TCR 254.
Heresies themselves do not condemn men, but an evil life; and also confirmations from the Word of the Falsities in the heresy... Explained.
This is why to confirm any false heretical thing is hurtful.
Beware of that execrable heresy...
So many heresies in the Christian world (an argument against the Divine Providence). Enumerated, Explained.
It follows that dissensions and heresies are inevitable...
(Thus) it may be seen whence come dissensions and heresies.
Still it is provided that anyone in any heresy as to the understanding can be reformed and saved, provided that... he does not confirm the false heretical things...
Who does not confirm his own heresy? Explained.
(This) is an insane heresy. Explained.
(This) is a cruel heresy. Explained.
Many things may be taken from the Word which at first appear to agree with the heresy... (Thus) a heretic can fascinate and obscure the understanding...
That the heresy of faith alone induces stupidity on hearts, etc. Signified.
A heresy destructive of the Church, because from the truths of the Word falsified. Signified.
That this heresy prevails and reigns through its reception by the laity. Signified.
That all the heresies which emanated from the Church of the Reformed were destroyed. Signified. AR 836, Signified.
Lest they should inspire something from their heresy... Signified.
Whence dissensions, heresies, etc.
One of them cried... It is heretical. Some... rejoined... It is not heretical; he adduces many passages of the Word...
They who teach false and heretical things... yet read the Word... may be compared to...
Heretical things have especially flowed from those who have been sensuous.
Various heresies... in which these three essentials... have been acknowledged...
Thence have been born direful heresies, one after another...
You can reject... this absurd and hurtful heresy...
He replied... Is not the Word the book of all heresies...
A single expression of the Word... can induce a whole false doctrine, or heresy, thus life...
Thus myriads of heresies can arise from the literal sense...
This opinion, or rather heresy, has prevailed in the universal Christian World...
This heresy answers to a sort of conjugial conjunction with a hermaphrodite.
This is the origin of all... the heresies in the Church. DWis 12. 2.
Evident from so many heresies within the Church, especially from the wicked Babylonish heresy, and from the Jewish heresy.
Heretical things are described in many places... by idols.
On all heresies, especially on (this one), there can be induced the appearance that they are from truths...
There are two things by which any heretical dogma can be confirmed: reasonings from the natural man, and confirmations from the sense of the letter. Signified by these two beasts.
The power of persuading and confirming any heresy from the Word...
All heresies, in so far as they are... falsifications of the Word, correspond to adulteries...
Evident from... the heresies etc. in general and in particular, both abroad and at home.
The reason the Word can be drawn to confirm heresies, unless it is read from doctrine, is that the sense of its letter consists of mere correspondences...
That thence there are so many heresies...
